title: Flatten and Rebuild Nested Structures
prompt:
Implement two operations over nested Python values. A value is either an integer, a list, a tuple, or a dictionary whose values are nested values. Dictionary traversal follows insertion order.

- `flatten(structure)` returns all integer leaves in depth-first order. Lists and tuples are visited left to right; dictionaries visit their values in insertion order.
- `unflatten(flat_list, structure)` returns a newly built value with the same container types, keys, and shape as `structure`, replacing every integer leaf with the next value from `flat_list`. Raise an error when the list is too short or has unused values after reconstruction.

Keep the input template unchanged. Empty containers have no leaves and retain their original container type.

Invalid inputs may be rejected with `assert`.

example.reasoning: The replacement order is exactly the order returned by flatten(template).
